title: Severe Cyclone Murasu 160 km from Nellore, due to cross Andhra coast near Ongole tonight
dek: The storm was 210 km southeast of Ongole at 8.30 am on Monday and is forecast to make landfall between 11.30 pm and 4 am with gusts of up to 120 kmph. Flights have been cancelled at Chennai and Vijayawada; Bengal faces only light rain.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was centred about 160 km east-southeast of Nellore, 180 km northeast of Chennai and 210 km southeast of Ongole at 8.30 am IST on Monday, moving west-northwest at about 22 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) bulletin as posted on X and reported by ETV Bharat. It is forecast to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on Monday, 2 November, and 4 am on Tuesday, 3 November, with sustained winds of 100 to 110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

The IMD has warned of a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide in low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh at landfall, with Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts most at risk. Five Andhra districts are under a red alert for extremely heavy rain. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab. There is still no weather warning for West Bengal, but the distant warning signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports has been raised.

## Latest bulletin

The storm moved quickly towards the coast overnight. At 2.30 am it was near latitude 13.6°N, longitude 82.5°E, about 330 km southeast of Ongole, the IMD said, according to Deccan Chronicle and Sakshi Post. At 5.30 am it was near 13.9°N, 81.8°E, and at 8.30 am near 14.1°N, 81.4°E, about 180 km east-southeast of Kavali and 240 km south of Machilipatnam, according to the IMD post reproduced by ETV Bharat. ETV Bharat said an IMD update at 11.03 am showed the storm still moving at 22 kmph.

"We are expecting very severe weather over Andhra Pradesh, particularly the coastal districts," S. Karuna Sagar, a scientist at the IMD's Amaravati centre, said, according to ETV Bharat. He warned of significant damage to crops and possible damage to roads and railway lines. 

A red cyclone warning, the last of the IMD's four stages, is in force for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining north Tamil Nadu coasts, according to OMMCOM. Red alerts for extremely heavy rain cover Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts, Sakshi Post reported, citing the IMD. East and West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu, Tirupati and Chittoor are on orange alert.

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority forecast district-average rain on Tuesday of about 179 mm in Eluru, 163 mm in Krishna, 161 mm in NTR and 147 mm in West Godavari, South First reported, and warned of heavy inflows into the Budameru.

After landfall the storm is forecast to weaken quickly to a deep depression by Tuesday evening and a depression by Wednesday morning as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, according to the IMD Kolkata bulletin issued at 10 pm on Sunday.

Fishing is suspended along the Andhra coast until Wednesday afternoon. The IMD has warned of local flooding, disruption to road and rail traffic, damage to kutcha houses, uprooted trees and damage to plantations, and asked authorities to move people out of vulnerable coastal settlements.

## Tamil Nadu

The storm's outer bands are bringing rain to northern Tamil Nadu. Parrys in Chennai recorded 149.2 mm in the 24 hours to 6 am on Monday, according to Greater Chennai Corporation figures reported by ETV Bharat. The corporation's commissioner, G. S. Sameeran, said two of the city's 22 subways had minor waterlogging that was soon cleared. Schools and colleges in Chennai and Tiruvallur are closed on Monday. Winds of 60-70 kmph are likely along the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coast from Monday evening.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cancelled a visit to Delhi planned for Monday because of the cyclone, his office said on X on Sunday afternoon. On Monday morning Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, reviewing preparations, named Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla and Krishna as the districts likely to be worst hit, and said six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and seven state disaster response teams were ready, his office said on X. He asked officials to move people out of low-lying areas and to stop movement near canals and streams. Three more NDRF teams left the force's 4th Battalion at Arakkonam in Tamil Nadu for Andhra Pradesh on Monday morning, ANI reported.

Vijayawada airport listed 10 IndiGo flights as cancelled on Monday, and Chennai airport said 11 flights had been cancelled as a precaution, according to posts reproduced by ETV Bharat. Schools and colleges are closed on Monday in NTR (Vijayawada), Palnadu and Nellore districts and in Gudur, ETV Bharat and Business Standard reported. The state health department said on Sunday it had set up 1,688 medical teams, 116 relief camps and 13,165 emergency beds, and readied 733 ambulances and 721 mobile medical units, South First reported.

The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101. Figures for the number of people evacuated had not been published by Monday afternoon.

## What it means for Bengal

The Kolkata bulletin says there is "at present no weather warning for West Bengal" linked to Murasu, which it is keeping under continuous watch. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island.

Light rain or thundershowers are likely in south Bengal on Monday and Tuesday, with light to moderate rain at one or two places in North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and the Midnapore districts on 3 November, and dry weather from 4 November, the bulletin said.

## Odisha braces again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. The IMD expects squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, along the south Odisha coast from Monday evening, rising to 50-60 kmph on Tuesday. IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. In Rayagada, all 11 fire station teams have been deployed and earthmovers stationed on two ghat sections of National Highway 326, and Malkangiri has shut schools and anganwadis from 2 to 4 November.

## What happens next

The IMD expects Murasu to reach the coast late on Monday night, with the strongest winds from around midnight until Tuesday noon. Many districts will feel the heaviest rain on Tuesday, after the storm has crossed the coast.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: south Andhra coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in low-lying south coastal Andhra Pradesh
- Distance from Ongole: about 330 km at 2.30 am Monday; 260 km at 5.30 am; 210 km at 8.30 am
- Red alert districts: Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
